summary: Point local retrieval legs at the derived-parallels artifact (retrieval_legs.py still walks live guru.db PARALLELS)
description:
PR #64 (derived-parallels/frozen-CONTRASTS split, todo:6da4f965) review
finding 9: after that PR, the shipped corpus and the local dev DB walk
different PARALLELS sets, and nothing in this repo points that out except
this ticket and the doc note that links here.

## What changed

scripts/export.py now excludes PARALLELS (and CONTRASTS) from load_edges()
and sources PARALLELS exclusively from the latest
scripts/derive_parallels.py run (load_derived_parallels()) — see
docs/ingest/16-derive-parallels.md. The live `edges` table in data/guru.db
still carries ~11,300 PARALLELS rows (the old Pass C output), untouched by
this change, because nothing deletes them and nothing was asked to.

## The divergence

guru/retrieval_legs.py still queries those live-table PARALLELS rows at
query time, in three places:

- line ~180 — the concept<->concept hop: `e.type IN ('PARALLELS',
  'DERIVES_FROM')` inside the HOP_DEPTH reachability query.
- line ~353 — the chunk<->chunk partner hop: `e.type IN ('PARALLELS',
  'CONTRASTS')`.
- line ~405 — score inheritance through PARALLELS (a chunk that PARALLELS
  a query-satisfying anchor inherits some of its rank).

None of these read scripts/derive_parallels.py's output. They are the old
Pass C edge set, produced by a different mechanism (LLM pair
classification vs. EXPRESSES x thin-student scoring), at different
weights, under a different tier.

## Concrete failure scenario

Someone runs `guru query` locally to tune EDGE_LEG/HOP_DEPTH behavior, or
benchmarks retrieval quality against data/guru.db. The results look
reasonable and get shipped as a tuning change or reported as a quality
finding — but production (guru-web, reading the exported corpus) is
serving a completely different PARALLELS supply built by a different
generator. The local measurement does not transfer, silently, because
nothing errors: both edge sets are well-formed PARALLELS rows, just from
different sources.

## Fix directions (either closes this)

1. Point retrieval_legs.py's three PARALLELS reads at the derived-parallels
   artifact (data/derived_parallels/<latest>/edges_derived.jsonl) instead
   of the live `edges` table — e.g. load it into an in-memory structure at
   query-harness startup, matching what export.py already does for the
   shipped corpus.
2. Materialize the deferred `derived_parallels` table in guru.db (explicitly
   called out as a future step in scripts/derive_parallels.py's module
   docstring and the rellm migration sketch it references) and point
   retrieval_legs.py at that table instead of `edges`. This is also the
   natural moment to decide whether the live `edges` PARALLELS rows should
   be dropped/archived once nothing reads them.

Not urgent — not a regression in PR #64 itself, but a new divergence that
PR created and didn't close. Reference: PR #64 review finding 9,
docs/ingest/16-derive-parallels.md ("Local retrieval divergence" note).
